stemBlocks.value: The diagram shows the straight line L. (a) State the coordinates of the point at which L cuts the y-axis. (b) State the coordinates of the point at which L cuts the x-axis. (c) Determine the gradient of L. (d) Hence write the equation of L in the form y = mx + c.
Think first: Read the two crossing points off the grid first; everything else follows from them.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p072-q10 from workbook page 72.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read where the line crosses the y-axis.

contentBlocks.value: The line meets the vertical axis 3 units above the origin

solutionSteps.instruction: Read where the line crosses the x-axis.

contentBlocks.value: The line meets the horizontal axis 3 units to the left of the origin

solutionSteps.instruction: Substitute the two points into the gradient formula.

contentBlocks.value: y = mx + c with m = 1 and c = 3

solutionSteps.instruction: Check with another point on the line.

contentBlocks.value: At x = 2 the line is at y = 5, and 2 + 3 = 5

strategyBlocks.value: Read the two intercepts from the diagram, use them in the gradient formula, then combine the gradient and the y-intercept into the equation.

whyThisWorks.value: The gradient counts how far the line rises for each unit it moves to the right, and using the two intercepts gives a rise of 3 over a run of 3. A positive gradient matches a line sloping upwards from left to right, which is a useful sanity check before any calculation. Once m and c are known the equation is fully determined, because a straight line is fixed by its steepness and its starting height on the y-axis.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the intercept as 3 instead of −3 by ignoring the direction along the x-axis.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the intercept as 3 instead of −3 by ignoring the direction along the x-axis.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the gradient as −1 because one of the differences is negative.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the gradient as −1 because one of the differences is negative.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the equation as y = 3x + 1, swapping the roles of m and c.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the equation as y = 3x + 1, swapping the roles of m and c.

examTip.value: Check the sign of your gradient against the picture: uphill left to right is positive, downhill is negative.
